newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Caricom criticizes proposed U.S. sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Caricom criticizes proposed U.S. sanctions.

text.p: Ambassadors of the Caribbean Community (Caricom) disagreed with a bill introduced in the U.S. Congress which would impose sanctions on Caricom if it moved closer to Havana.

A report in The Sunday Observer newspaper said Caricom's ambassadors to Washington delivered a letter denouncing the proposal to the bill's sponsor, Florida Republican Rep. Ileana Ros-Lehtinen, on Friday.
The ambassadors said "Cuba is a Caribbean nation and part of the Western Hemisphere," and lamented "the threat to sovereign governments" contained in the bill.

The bill would allow President Bill Clinton to withhold aid and block U.S. investments to Caricom or the Central American Common Market if either admitted Cuba. The bill also proposed denying tariff benefits to any country which signed a free-trade pact with Cuba.
The bill "contravenes the norms of international law -- including World Trade Organization rules," the letter said.

Trinidad Foreign Minister Ralph Maraj earlier this month said Caricom intends to raise the matter when Caricom foreign ministers meet Secretary of State Madeleine Albright in Barbados. No date has been set for that meeting.
Cuba has not officialy requested membership in Caricom, but a Caricom-Cuba commission scheduled to meet in December will discuss a proposed free trade accord between Havana and the region.
Caricom's 15 members include the independent English-speaking states of the region, plus Surinam and Haiti.
